gen-gf-phudu-gf-kumbh-sans: Kumbh Sans keeps its terminals cut short of the bowl, drawn like a fixed pen moving across the page. And Phudu is the loud one, its curves flung open, while the body text simply gets on with the sentence.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-lato: Blunt, friendly, a bit cheeky: Phudu draws each letter with one constant line, like a ballpoint. Lato follows with wide s curves barely curled in, and that quiet openness is what ties them together.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-libre-franklin: Phudu draws every letter with a flat, unvarying line and wide-open curve endings, a bold and distinctive look. Libre Franklin adds its splayed c terminal beneath.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-line-seed-jp: Approachable from the first line, LINE Seed JP sets horizontals exactly as heavy as verticals, with counters the eye slips through. Phudu does the shouting; this sans does the talking.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-livvic: Approachable describes Livvic, whose curves carry no stress and whose c opens generously beneath the bold, distinctive Phudu heading. Both draw their lines plainly, so the two fit together.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-lunasima: Lunasima keeps its c tips well apart, never creeping toward touching. Under Phudu's heavy display lettering, whose horizontals match its verticals, a longer passage would read cleanly and contemporary, with room for the eye.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-lxgw-marker-gothic: Phudu draws everything with one fixed nib width, bold and distinctive, with generous openings on every curve. But LXGW Marker Gothic softens things below, its wide-open c and gentle pencil-like weight shift making a friendlier second voice.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-m-plus-1: Generous terminal openings on every curve make Phudu instantly recognizable, a bold display with a ballpoint's plain line. M PLUS 1 then offers big open eyes on every e and a, a fineliner-flat sans-serif for the actual reading.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-m-plus-1p: Phudu keeps a quiet, level beat, with no accents of weight. M PLUS 1p, a plain sans open at every curve end, follows it well, and a body size a notch or two above default would suit it.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-m-plus-2: M PLUS 2 has a gaping c opening and one fixed nib width. Phudu is best at making a bold, distinctive statement up top, while this plain sans is best at approachable, professional running text.
